package_info.package_name: npm registry (infrastructure-wide breach, not a single package)
package_info.why_malicious: The breach involved the theft of OAuth tokens, AWS keys, and plaintext credentials, enabling unauthorized access to private repositories and sensitive user data. The attacker exfiltrated usernames, password hashes, emails, and private package metadata, representing a severe compromise of npm's security and user trust.

execution_context.file_location: OAuth app tokens issued to Heroku and Travis-CI

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Use of stolen OAuth tokens to authenticate to npm and GitHub APIs, enabling download of private repositories.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Attacker used stolen OAuth tokens to access and download private npm repositories and metadata.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: OAuth tokens are intended for authorized app access; use by an attacker is inherently malicious.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal use expects tokens to be used only by the app/user they were issued to, not by an attacker.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: OAuth tokens are legitimately used by CI/CD systems to automate repository access.
key_indicators: Unusual access patterns from OAuth tokens
Tokens issued to Heroku/Travis-CI used outside expected context

execution_context.file_location: AWS access key in private npm repositories

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Use of compromised AWS access key to escalate privileges and access npm production infrastructure.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Attacker used a stolen AWS key (found in private repos) to gain deeper access to npm's production systems.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: AWS keys should never be exposed in repositories; use by an attacker is a critical security incident.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: AWS keys are expected to be secret and used only by authorized infrastructure components.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: AWS keys are used for legitimate infrastructure automation, but never exposed in code.
key_indicators: AWS key found in code or repo
AWS key used from unusual IPs or locations
Access to production infrastructure outside normal automation

execution_context.trigger: Internal logging (post-integration of npm into GitHub)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Plaintext npm access tokens, passwords, and GitHub Personal Access Tokens stored in internal logs.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Sensitive credentials were inadvertently logged in plaintext, creating a risk of internal misuse or exposure.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Credentials should never be logged in plaintext; this creates a risk of insider threat or accidental exposure.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal logging should redact or avoid sensitive credential data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Debug logs may sometimes capture sensitive data during troubleshooting, but this is a security anti-pattern.
key_indicators: Presence of access tokens or passwords in logs
No redaction or encryption of sensitive fields

attack_chain.action: Attacker obtains stolen OAuth tokens issued to Heroku and Travis-CI.
attack_chain.leads_to: Use tokens to access private npm repositories.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses OAuth tokens to download private repositories and metadata.
attack_chain.leads_to: Discovery of AWS access key in private repositories.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses compromised AWS access key to escalate privileges and access npm production infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of sensitive user and package data from npm cloud storage.

attack_chain.action: Attacker exfiltrates usernames, password hashes, emails, and private package metadata.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential for account takeover and further attacks.

attack_chain.action: Plaintext credentials found in internal logs (not directly used in this attack, but a separate risk).
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential for insider misuse or future compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Unusual OAuth token usage patterns (accessing many private repos in a short time)
AWS keys used from unexpected IPs or geographies
Bulk download of private repository data
Sensitive credentials appearing in internal logs
file_indicators: AWS access keys present in code or configuration files
Internal logs containing plaintext tokens or passwords
network_indicators: OAuth token authentication from new or suspicious IPs
Large data transfers from npm infrastructure to external IPs
AWS API calls from non-standard locations
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unusual OAuth token activity, especially tokens issued to CI/CD systems accessing private repositories. Alert on AWS keys found in code or used from new locations. Scan internal logs for plaintext credentials and ensure proper redaction. Watch for large or unexpected data exfiltration from npm infrastructure.
